paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two example selection methods, ST-ES and Random, in relation to the number of in-context examples. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Examples", has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 8, and has tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled "minADE$_{20}$", has a linear scale, ranges from 21.00 to 24.00, and has tick labels at intervals of 0.50. The plot compares two lines: the blue line representing ST-ES starts at approximately 24.00 on the y-axis when the x-axis is 0, decreases sharply to around 22.00 at x=1, continues to decrease to about 21.10 at x=7, and then slightly increases to 21.20 at x=8; the orange line representing Random starts at around 24.20 on the y-axis when x=0, remains relatively steady around 24.00 until x=5, and then gradually decreases to approximately 23.70 at x=8, with both lines having a solid style and circular markers.
model_annotations.German: The plot compares the performance of two example selection methods, ST-ES and Random, in terms of minADE20 as the number of in-context examples varies. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Examples", has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 8, and has tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled "minADE20", has a linear scale, ranges from 21.00 to 24.00, and has tick labels at intervals of 0.5. The blue line representing ST-ES starts at approximately 24.00 on the y-axis when the number of examples is 0, decreases sharply to around 22.00 at 2 examples, and continues to decrease more gradually to about 21.10 at 7 examples, before slightly increasing to 21.20 at 8 examples. The orange line representing Random starts at approximately 24.10 on the y-axis, remains relatively steady around 24.00 until 5 examples, and then gradually decreases to about 23.70 at 8 examples.
